question: Against a backdrop dominated by the conflict in the Middle East and the resultant doubling of the price of aviation fuel in recent months, various airlines are announcing potential fare increases and the introduction of new surcharges to offset their rising operating costs.

In this connection, and given the fact that some airlines are informing passengers at the time of purchase, or after booking in some cases, that the final ticket price may vary in the run-up to the flight depending on fluctuations in the cost of aviation fuel, can the Commission say: 1.

Whether it considers this practice of altering the final ticket price, and adding a surcharge once the ticket has already been bought and paid for, to be in breach of the rules governing air passenger rights, consumer protection and price transparency, which are binding on airlines?
If not, whether it plans to take measures to ensure legal certainty for passengers and prevent abusive practices that entail passing fuel price increases on to consumers?
Whether it intends to address this issue in the forthcoming review of Regulation (EC) No 1008/2008 on common rules for the operation of air services?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.6.2026) 1. The rules on transparent pricing of air tickets in Regulation (EC) No 1008/20081 require that the final ticket price must be displayed at all times when offering or publishing air fares to the general public. As this obligation applies explicitly to the final ticket price to be paid, any retroactive change of the price is excluded.

Airlines may not include terms and conditions which would allow them to increase the price of the ticket above what is advertised at the time of purchase simply because fuel was more expensive than they had accounted for. 2. The Commission adopted on 8 May 2026 guidance2 on issues relating to aviation fuel in the context of current price increases and potential supply issues, to ensure legal certainty.

In the first instance, it is for the price transparency authorities in the Member States to enforce the rules. 3. The Commission is looking at several issues relating to price transparency as part of the review of Regulation (EC) No 1008/2008.
